name: Grade 8 IIT: Arduino Circuit Basics
description: Arduino and Freenove kit parts, breadboard connections, pins, power, ground, resistors, LEDs, sketches, upload, delay, serial monitor, and troubleshooting.

words.definition: A microcontroller platform used to build electronic projects.
An electronics kit with parts and guides for projects.
words.example: The Freenove kit included LEDs and sensors.

words.definition: A small computer on a board that controls inputs and outputs.
A board used to build temporary circuits without soldering.
words.example: The LED was placed on the breadboard.

words.definition: A connection point on a board.
words.example: The LED connected to a digital pin.

words.definition: A breadboard line often used for power or ground.
Electrical energy used by a circuit.
words.example: The circuit needed power and ground.

words.definition: The reference or return point in a circuit, often labeled GND.
words.example: The resistor connected back to ground.

words.definition: A component that limits electrical current.
A small light controlled by a circuit or program.
words.example: The LED blinked after the sketch uploaded.

words.definition: The correct positive and negative direction for a component.
words.example: The LED did not work when polarity was reversed.
The Blink sketch changed delay values.

words.definition: To send code to the board.

words.example: Changing delay changed the blink pattern.

words.definition: A tool that displays data sent from the board.
words.example: The Serial Monitor showed sensor readings.

words.definition: To find and fix the cause of a problem.
words.example: The group troubleshot the missing ground wire.

words.definition: A labeled drawing that shows connections.
words.example: The diagram labeled 5V, GND, and pins.

words.definition: An ordered set of steps or outputs.
words.example: The flowing LED sequence moved from left to right.
